scope: 98 PE-pool edge cases; endpoint security engineer perspective
method: Static analysis only: atomscan/cleave facts, Rizin disassembly, Ghidra decompilation, JADX for misfiled Android APK, and offline cryptographic reconstruction. No specimen executed and no specimen endpoints contacted.

reverse_review.reason: Conceals an external URL, fetches and decodes remote content into temporary HTML and drives browser execution. No disclosed administrative or user-selected workflow explains the concealed code-loading chain.
Recovered hex/RC4/custom-XOR shellcode and embedded DLL. DLL starts a worker on load, fingerprints the endpoint, retrieves encoded remote stages and maps/executed code in memory.

Rotates concealed strings, installs keyboard/window hooks and selects application login controls; recovered credential field selectors and operator-controlled HTTP credential collectors establish theft intent.

Recovered embedded executable by compacting stride-3 data and reconstructing a modified RC4 state-overwrite cipher (argument low byte 0x33). Loader patches a native mapping API, manually maps/relocates payload and executes its entry point through a decoy module load. Recovered payload adds covert remote-control capabilities.

Pattern-scans game process memory and installs inline call patches that copy application strings/state into private buffers. Encodes those buffers into HTTP queries, transmits them and processes server responses. Global Windows hooks alone were not evidence of keyboard theft: their callbacks merely chain.

Ghidra/Rizin recover an IOCTL handler that writes a caller-supplied address into a selected SSDT entry while bypassing/restoring CR0 write protection. No autonomous hook target, payload or hide routine was established; anti-rootkit restoration and rootkit modification are both possible.

Ghidra recovers an IOCTL-selected process killer using kernel process attachment and native termination. No autonomous security-product target or concealed payload is present; highly dangerous dual-use helper, intent unresolved.
